dedupe_keys.name: earth library spectral endmembers and mapping tools

description: Earth Library is a Python package with a global reference library of spectral endmembers for satellite land-cover mapping. Its maintained README describes vegetation, bare soil, urban material and burned-material spectra from visible to shortwave-infrared wavelengths, plus resampling and mixture-analysis tools. Users select endmembers and sensor bands; outputs help estimate land-cover fractions from imagery. Geographic coverage follows the satellite observations and reference-library suitability. GitHub metadata states MIT licensing. The README says Earth Engine routines are currently out of date, though the spectral library is unaffected. A limitation is that a global spectral reference may not represent every local material or atmospheric correction, so mapped land cover needs independent checks. The package can prepare urban surface and vegetation inputs for heat, runoff or transport simulations. QGIS in the catalogue is a general GIS platform. No spectral library data or package was downloaded.
